answer: In an agent economy, sybil attacks can be resisted by requiring each agent to post a collateral bond into a communal harbor. This harbor serves as the kernel of economic security: funds are locked until the agent proves unique liveness by broadcasting a cryptographically signed beacon derived from a scarce real-world resource such as a hardware enclave or time-locked puzzle. Duplicate identities fail the beacon uniqueness check and forfeit their bond, making mass fake accounts prohibitively expensive.
